newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM criticises reported Uruguay deal.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM criticises reported Uruguay deal.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Thursday stepped into a controversy about Uruguay's release of two rebels linked to the group which staged the Lima hostage siege, saying the action did not help negotiations.
"The Uruguay government has explained that there was no link between the two (release of the two rebels and the Lima hostage issue)," Hashimoto told reporters.
"I don't know whether this is true or not, but in any case it has made a solution of the case difficult," Hashimoto said. "We must not surrender to terrorism."
More than 100 hostages remain confined in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by armed Marxist guerrillas, who stormed the residence on December 17.
But the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas freed Uruguay's ambassador to Peru on Tuesday following the Uruguay government's release from prison of two of their fellow members.
Uruguay denied it had negotiated a swap, but a well-placed Uruguayan government source told Reuters a deal was struck.
Peru recalled its top diplomat in Uruguay on Wednesday in apparent protest.

Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama, Japan's top government spokesman, declined to comment on whether there was disagreement between countries on the release of Uruguayan ambassador Tobare Bocalandro Yapeyu.
"I will refrain from commenting immediately on any assumption or on whether there has been disagreement among countries concerned," Kajiyama told a news conference.
